title: Back up your AI agent so you never lose its memory (and move it to a new computer)
summary: If your agent runs on your own computer or server, its memory, chats, automations and logins live in a folder that one crash could wipe. OpenClaw has a built-in backup and restore, and one user just moved 9 agents and 800+ sessions to a bigger server with 11 minutes of downtime.
what_the_bot_does: Pauses the agent so nothing changes while the backup is made.
Packs its settings, memory files, chat history, automations and saved logins into one checked backup file.
Restores that file on a new computer or server into a fresh folder, without touching anything live.
Runs a health check, then starts the agent again so conversations pick up where they left off.
what_you_end_up_with: A tested backup file of your agent you can restore any time, or the same agent running on a new machine with its memory and automations intact.

tools.note: Built-in 'openclaw backup create' and 'openclaw backup restore'
Back up its folder the same way; check its docs for the exact steps

prompt: Help me back up my [OpenClaw] agent safely. Walk me through it one step at a time in plain words: stop it, make a verified backup file, and tell me where the file is. Then help me test restoring it into an empty folder so I know the backup works. Don't delete or overwrite anything from my current setup, and don't print any API keys or passwords on screen.
setup: Find where your agent keeps its data. For OpenClaw, run 'openclaw status' to see the folder (usually ~/.openclaw).
Stop the agent first ('openclaw gateway stop'), then make a checked backup: 'openclaw backup create --output ~/Backups/openclaw --verify'.
Copy the backup file somewhere safe: an external drive or private cloud storage. It contains your keys and logins, so treat it like a password.
To move: install the same OpenClaw version on the new machine, run 'openclaw backup restore <file> --target ~/openclaw-restored', point OpenClaw at it, then run 'openclaw doctor' and restart.
Do a quick test chat and check your automations ran before you switch off the old machine.
watch_out: The backup holds API keys, logins and chat history. Store it encrypted or somewhere private, never in a public folder.
OpenClaw's docs say to stop the agent before backing up, because copying files while it runs can save a broken database.
Restoring old chat-app logins (like WhatsApp) can get out of sync; you may need to reconnect them. Plugins also need reinstalling.
If you're retiring an old server, it's a good time to change your API keys (OpenClaw migration guide).
